# Transformer Attention: Explanation & NumPy Implementation

## The Core Idea

In a sequence model (language, image patches, etc.), **attention** lets each position look at every other position and decide *how much* to focus on each one. Unlike RNNs that process tokens left-to-right with a fixed-size hidden state, attention is fully parallel: every token simultaneously queries the entire context.

The three tensors in play are:

| Tensor | Shape (per head) | Role |
|--------|-----------------|------|
| **Q** – Queries | `(seq_len, d_k)` | "What am I looking for?" |
| **K** – Keys | `(seq_len, d_k)` | "What do I contain / can I match against?" |
| **V** – Values | `(seq_len, d_v)` | The actual content that gets retrieved |

The output at position *i* is a **weighted average of all V vectors**, where the weights come from how well Q_i matches each K_j.
